summary: A connectivity group offering mobile service, home broadband, television and enterprise networks, with businesses in India and overseas.
description: Bharti Airtel builds and operates networks that let households and businesses communicate and use digital services. Customers pay for continuing access, while the network requires spectrum, equipment, energy, maintenance and investment.
money: Revenue comes from subscriptions, usage and enterprise services. Customer numbers, spending, retention and service mix matter alongside network running costs, spectrum obligations and capital investment.
customers: Mobile users, households, enterprises and wholesale/network customers across the relevant markets and group entities.
drivers: Average spending, customer quality and retention, broadband adoption, enterprise demand, network investment, regulation and currency.

groups.title: Mobile connectivity
groups.examples: Prepaid and postpaid mobile plans and data services.
groups.explanation: The customer pays for service over time. More data consumption does not automatically produce the same increase in revenue.

groups.title: Homes and television
groups.examples: Home broadband, wireless home access where offered and digital television.
groups.explanation: Installation, network reach, household adoption and retention influence these economics.

groups.title: Enterprise and network services
groups.examples: Airtel Business connectivity and related solutions for organisations.
groups.explanation: A corporate network contract has different service obligations, pricing and credit terms from an individual prepaid plan.

groups.title: Overseas operations and related services
groups.examples: African mobile and mobile-money activities and other relevant group operations.
groups.explanation: Country conditions, currencies, licences and entity ownership affect the consolidated result; an India plan does not represent the whole group.

basics.title: A network must be funded before and during use
basics.text: Spectrum gives rights to use radio frequencies; equipment and fibre carry the service. Licence rights and installed capability do not themselves guarantee paying customer demand.

steps.title: Secure rights and build coverage
steps.text: Arrange spectrum and network infrastructure under the relevant regulatory permissions.

steps.title: Connect customers
steps.text: Sell and activate plans, connections or enterprise services through appropriate channels.

steps.title: Operate reliably
steps.text: Maintain coverage, capacity, service quality, energy and security as traffic grows.

steps.title: Collect and reinvest
steps.text: Service receipts must cover operations, financing and the next round of network spending.

specifics.title: ARPU is an average
specifics.text: Average revenue per user can change through tariffs, plan mix and the mix of customers. Read the definition and geography; a higher average does not say every user pays more.

specifics.title: Cash needs go beyond operating earnings
specifics.text: Network upgrades, spectrum payments and leases require funding. EBITDA is not cash left after these requirements.

specifics.title: India and overseas results need currency discipline
specifics.text: Local growth and the rupee result can diverge because of exchange rates. Mobile-money balances and customer activity measures are also different from earned revenue.

watch: Are customers staying and paying for useful service?

Read active-customer definitions, additions and churn with ARPU and service quality. Churn means customers leaving; compare the same geography and period rather than mixing group and India mobile measures.
What drives the change in average spending?
Tariffs and customer mix can affect ARPU.
Compare tariff actions, prepaid/postpaid mix and usage with the company’s ARPU definition. Separate more paying users from higher revenue per user; neither alone explains the whole earnings change.
Does network spending improve useful capacity?

Read capital expenditure, deployment, utilisation and quality alongside customer growth and cash flow. Spectrum purchase, payment timing, leases and network equipment can have different accounting and cash effects.
Are homes and enterprise services expanding sensibly?
Follow broadband adoption, enterprise revenue and relevant costs and receivables. A connection passed by the network is different from an activated paying household.
How do country and ownership changes affect the group?

Read local-currency and reported growth, country risks, subsidiary interests and consolidation changes. Do not replace Bharti Airtel’s group figures with Airtel Africa’s local statement or an India-mobile metric.
risks: Rivals can influence tariffs, acquisition costs and customer movement.
Spectrum, network upgrades and leases can use substantial cash even during profitable operations.
Licence conditions, cybersecurity, outages and compliance failures can affect trust and operations.
Inflation, political conditions and exchange movements can alter overseas performance and reported earnings.
context: A bundled household is still several operating jobs

A customer can buy mobile, home connectivity and television together. Bundling may support retention, but the company still has to install, operate and support the underlying services at an acceptable cost.
quiz: Is EBITDA the money available after paying for all network expansion?
No. Depreciation, financing, taxes, spectrum, leases and capital spending need separate examination. EBITDA and free cash available are different measures.

financialNotes.title: Match service, country and measurement basis
financialNotes.text: The table preserves the audited segment definitions and separates segment sums from consolidated revenue after internal-sales eliminations. The reported earnings measure comes before financing, exceptional items and tax. Do not combine India customer-spending averages, Africa revenue and a group EBITDA margin into an invented profit calculation.
